headlines.title: Johnson & Johnson to Host Enterprise Business Review
headlines.summary: NEW BRUNSWICK, N.J., October 27, 2026--Johnson & Johnson (NYSE: JNJ) will hold an Enterprise Business Review for the investment community on Tuesday, December 8th, 2026. During the event, Company leaders will provide a detailed review of the Innovative Medicine and MedTech businesses, highlight how their pipelines are shaping the future of healthcare, and discuss the Company’s long-term strategy for delivering the next wave of growth and shareholder value.

headlines.title: Your Pension Still Pays the Same $3,100 It Did the Day You Retired. These 3 ETFs Give You the Raise It Never Will
headlines.summary: A pension check that freezes the moment you retire quietly loses ground every year as prices climb around it. Three funds approach this problem from different angles, and how you combine them changes everything.

headlines.title: What Do Johnson & Johnson (JNJ) Cancer Trial Wins Mean For Its Stock?
headlines.summary: Johnson & Johnson (NYSE: JNJ) reported new oncology data, including a 75% tumor response rate for JNJ-6143 in advanced prostate cancer. The RYBREVANT FASPRO regimen produced a 77% response rate as an initial treatment option in advanced head and neck cancer patients. ERLEADA use around surgery reduced recurrence and death risk in high risk prostate cancer, while an orthopedics merger with Smith & Nephew collapsed over leadership disagreements.

headlines.title: ORIC Pharmaceuticals Sinks 22% as J&J Presents Rival Prostate Cancer Data
headlines.summary: Key TakeawaysORIC Pharmaceuticals shares fell 22% today after Johnson & Johnson presented early data for JNJ-6143, a rival prostate cancer drug. The drop looks too big, since J&J’s data comes from a small early-stage study and ORIC’s own prostate cancer drug is already in a Phase 3 trial.

headlines.title: 2 Safe S&P 500 Dividend Stocks Boomers Can Buy and Hold Forever
headlines.summary: One of these household-name S&P 500 stocks has raised its dividend every single year for seven decades, and both pay their checks from cash left over after covering every other business need. Here is what stands between them and an eighth decade of raises.

description: Johnson & Johnson, together with its subsidiaries, engages in the research and development, manufacture, and sale of a range of products in the healthcare field worldwide. It operates in two segments, Innovative Medicine and MedTech. The Innovative Medicine segment offers products for various therapeutic areas, such as oncology, immunology, neuroscience, pulmonary hypertension, infectious diseases, and cardiovascular and metabolism distributed through retailers, wholesalers, distributors, hospitals, and healthcare professionals for prescription use. The MedTech segment provides a portfolio of products used in the surgery, orthopedic, cardiovascular, and vision fields distributed through wholesalers, hospitals and retailers, and used in the professional fields by physicians, nurses, hospitals, eye care professionals and clinics. This segment also offers products and enabling technologies that support joint reconstruction, trauma, spine, sports related injuries, and others, as well as open, laparoscopic, and robotic surgical procedures; instrumentation, energy devices, stapling systems, wound closure, biosurgery products, and digital and robotic technologies; breast aesthetics and reconstruction; contact lenses under the ACUVUE brand; intraocular lenses for cataract surgery, and other products used in cataract and refractive procedures under the TECNIS brand. The company was founded in 1886 and is based in New Brunswick, New Jersey.
